Thanks for the clear list. A few clarifying Qs before we lock a workshop time:

1) For SAML, do you require IdP-initiated, SP-initiated, or both for the control plane? Our SSO team turns on SP-initiated by default for admin portals.

3) Role granularity — our security team prefers a separate RBAC role for "service-account" vs "machine" vs human accounts. Can you map SCIM groups to multiple policy bindings in PrivCP?

Forwarding Maria's questions — short internal notes below before the workshop: 

- SAML modes: we support both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated. For Private Control Plane, SP-initiated is safer for audit (session creation is logged at our SP). Need to confirm what Clearwater will enable.
- SCIM attributes: we can drop non-essential PII; recommended minimum set: userName, externalId, active, emails[type=work], groups. The attached scim_schema_v2.json is our guidance.
- Role mapping: PrivCP supports group -> policy binding with multiple bindings per group. For machine/service accounts we typically recommend a separate SCIM attribute (entitlements or custom:roles) so we can avoid brittle group splits.

Dev — can you validate the plan to accept a provisioning service account token + SCIM push, and confirm any constraints on group nesting and custom attributes? Also need a short note on how we will populate service-account principals in PrivCP (IAM role creation flow).

Thanks — Jonas

Subject: Re: Fwd: PrivCP identity & access: hybrid SAML/SCIM mapping and operational checklist

Jonas / team —

Quick technical plan (high level):

1) SCIM provisioning: we support v2 SCIM push using a bearer token tied to a dedicated SCIM service account. Permissions required: Users.ReadWrite, Groups.ReadWrite. We will accept the following attributes (subset): userName, id/externalId, active, displayName, emails[type], entitlements (string array), and groups (array of group ids).

2) Group -> IAM mapping: our control plane exposes an internal mapping table where a SCIM group ID maps to one or more IAM policy bindings. We allow multiple bindings per group (so group X can map to both read-only and usage-cost-alert roles via separate bindings). No nested-group evaluation at present; we can accept pre-flattened groups from the IdP.

3) Service accounts: recommended process — customer creates a SCIM-only service account inside their IdP and sends us the client id/secret (or an outbound IP-locked token). We will create a corresponding PrivCP service principal and mark it with the "machine" principal type. That principal is excluded from user-centric SSO flows and uses token-based auth for provisioning API.

4) SAML modes: we will default to SP-initiated for admin console access and support IdP-initiated for SSO links if Clearwater wants it. We will log assertion IDs and relay state in our audit events.

5) Minimal PII: we will ignore any extra profile fields. Our SCIM ingest drops fields not listed in the schema. Good to keep payload small for compliance.

I'll add a short implementation checklist to SEC-3123 (https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SEC-3123) and attach the scim_schema_v2.json here.

—Dev
